blocks.content: Thermal convection currents operating in the mantle are generated by radioactive decay and primordial heat, driving the movement of lithospheric plates above.

rows: Negative buoyancy of sinking dense oceanic lithosphere
Gravitational sliding down elevated ridge slopes

items: Slab pull is recognized as the most powerful single force driving plate motion, exceeding ridge push and basal drag in magnitude.
Arthur Holmes proposed the thermal convection current hypothesis in 1930, decades before the comprehensive theory of Plate Tectonics was accepted in the 1960s.
Divergent boundaries are associated with mantle upwelling and ridge push, while convergent boundaries feature subduction and slab pull.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Arthur Holmes in the 1930s first proposed thermal convection currents in the mantle as the primary driving mechanism behind tectonic plate movement.
Convective currents are generated by heat originating from radioactive decay and residual primordial heat within the Earth's mantle and core.
The semi-fluid, ductile asthenosphere allows rigid lithospheric plates to float, drift, and slide across its surface.
Slab pull occurs at subduction zones where colder, denser oceanic lithosphere sinks into the mantle under gravity, pulling the trailing plate along.
Ridge push operates at mid-ocean ridges where newly formed, hot, and elevated oceanic crust slides gravitationally away from the ridge crest.
